newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil moves up signing of cellular accords - source.
newsitem.headline: Brazil moves up signing of cellular accords - source.

text.p: The Brazilian government will sign contracts for B Band cellular concessions more quickly than planned as a way to speed up the sector's privatization, an official source said.

A Communications Ministry source said the deadline for signing the contracts is now 10 working days after the auction winner is announced instead of 30 business days, as originally set out in bid specifications published last month.

The change in the B Band tender documents "signals the government's desire to move ahead as quickly as possible" with the cellular sector's transfer to private hands, said the source, who requested anonymity.
The government will take bids April 7 on its 10 B Band concession areas nationwide, kicking off the privatization of Brazil's telecom sector.
The B Band sell-off has drawn the interest of the world's largest cellular telephone operators, who are seeking a foothold in Brazil's promising telecommunications market.

Bid specifications released in January set base prices totalling 3.69 billion reais, including 600 million a piece for two Sao Paulo concessions and 500 million reais for Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states.
